verses.sanskrit: वासुदेव उवाच । शृणु कौन्तेय रामस्य प्रभावो यो मया श्रुतः । महर्षीणां कथयतां विक्रमं तस्य जन्म च ॥१॥
verses.english: Yudhisthira said In this world, O Bharata, good and bad acts attach themselves to man for the purpose of producing fruits for enjoyment or endurance.

verses.sanskrit: यथा च जामदग्न्येन कोटिशः क्षत्रिया हताः । उद्भूता राजवंशेषु ये भूयो भारते हताः ॥२॥
verses.english: Is man, however, to be regarded as their doer or is he not to be considered so? My mind is full of doubts regarding this question. I wish to hear this fully from you, O grandfather.

verses.sanskrit: जह्नोरजस्तु तनयो बलाकाश्वस्तु तत्सुतः । कुशिको नाम धर्मज्ञस्तस्य पुत्रो महीपते ॥३॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Regarding it, О Yudhisthira, is cited the old discourse between Prahlada and Indra.

verses.sanskrit: अग्र्यं तपः समातिष्ठत्सहस्राक्षसमो भुवि । पुत्रं लभेयमजितं त्रिलोकेश्वरमित्युत ॥४॥
verses.english: The king of the Daityas, viz., Prahlada, was unattached to all worldly objects. His sins had been dissipated. Of respectable parentage, he was endued with great learning. Free from stupefaction and pride, ever pervaded by the quality of goodness, and devoted to various vows, he considered praise and censure in the same light. Endued with self-control he was then passing his time in an empty room. Conversant with the origin and the destruction of all created objects mobile and immobile, he was never angry with things that displeased him and never rejoiced at the acquisition of agreeable objects. He considered equally gold and a clod of earth.

verses.sanskrit: तमुग्रतपसं दृष्ट्वा सहस्राक्षः पुरन्दरः । समर्थं पुत्रजनने स्वयमेवान्वपद्यत ॥५॥
verses.english: Earnestly studying the Soul and acquiring Emancipation, and firm in knowledge, he had acquired firm conclusions about truth.

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रत्वमगमद्राजंस्तस्य लोकेश्वरेश्वरः । गाधिर्नामाऽभवत्पुत्रः कौशिकः पाकशासनः ॥६॥
verses.english: Acquainted with what is supreme and what is not so among all things, omniscient and of universal sight, as he was seated on day in a solitary room with his senses under complete control, Shakra approached him, and desirous

verses.sanskrit: तस्य कन्याऽभवद्राजन्नाम्ना सत्यवती प्रभो । तां गाधिर्भुगुपुत्राय सर्चीकाय ददौ प्रभुः ॥७॥
verses.english: O king, I see all those qualities permanently living in you by which a person acquires the esteem of all.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याः प्रीतः स शौचेन भार्गवः कुरुनन्दन । पुत्रार्थं श्रपयामास चरुं गाधेस्तथैव च ॥८॥
verses.english: Your understanding seems to be like that of a child, free from attachment and aversion. You know the soul. What, do you think, is the best means by which a knowledge of the Soul may be acquired.

verses.sanskrit: आहूयोवाच तां भार्यां सर्चीको भार्गवस्तदा । उपभोज्यश्चरुरयं त्वया मात्राऽप्ययं तव ॥९॥
verses.english: You are now bound in fetters, fallen off from your former position, brought under the sway of your foes, and divested of prosperity. Your present circumstances are such as may well give room to grief. Yet how is it, O Prahlada, that you do not grieve.
verses.bhavadeepa: गाधेः पुत्रार्थं तस्याश्च पुत्रार्थं चरुं चरुद्वयम् ॥८॥

verses.sanskrit: तस्या जनिष्यते पुत्रो दीप्तिमान्क्षत्रियर्षभः । अजय्यः क्षत्रियैर्लोके क्षत्रियर्षभसूदनः ॥१०॥
verses.english: Is this owing, O son of Diti, to the acquisition of wisdom or is it on account of your fortitude? Behold your calamities, O Prahlada, and yet you appear like one that is happy and tranquil.

verses.sanskrit: तवापि पुत्रं कल्याणि धृतिमन्तं शमात्मकम् । तपोऽन्वितं द्विजश्रेष्ठं चरुरेष विधास्यति ॥११॥
verses.english: Thus urged by Indra, the king of the Daityas, endued with firinness and with fixed conclusions about truth, replied in these sweet words showing great wisdom.

verses.sanskrit: इत्येवमुक्त्वा तां भार्यां सर्चीको भृगुनन्दनः । तपस्यभिरतः श्रीमाञ्जगामारण्यमेव हि ॥१२॥
verses.english: Prahlada said “He who does not know the origin and the destruction of all created objects, is, on account of such ignorance, stupefied. He, however, who knows these two things, is never stupefied.

verses.sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु तीर्थयात्रापरो नृपः । गाधिः सदारः सम्प्राप्तः सर्चीकस्याश्रमं प्रति ॥१३॥
verses.english: All kinds of entities and non-entities come into being or cease on account of their own nature. No kind of personal exertion is necessary (for their production). In the absence of personal exertion it is clear that no personal agent exists for the production of all this that we perceive. But though the person never does anything, yet through the influence of Ignorance a consciousness regarding agency over spreads itself on it.

verses.sanskrit: चरुद्वयं गृहीत्वा च राजन्सत्यवती तदा । भर्तुर्वाक्यं तदा व्यग्रा मात्रे हृष्टा न्यवेदयत् ॥१४॥
verses.english: He who regards himself as the doer of good or bad acts possesses a vile wisdom. Such a person is, in my opinion, does not know the truth.

verses.sanskrit: माता तु तस्याः कौन्तेय दुहित्रे स्वं चरुं ददौ । तस्याश्चरुमथाज्ञानादात्मसंस्थं चकार ह ॥१५॥
verses.english: If, O Shakra, the being known as person were really the actor, then all acts undertaken for his own benefit would certainly be successful. None of those acts would be futile. Persons struggling their utmost to avoid what is not desired and to bring about what is desired are not to be seen. What becomes then of personal exertion?

verses.sanskrit: अथ सत्यवती गर्भं क्षत्रियान्तकरं तदा । धारयामास दीप्तेन वपुषा घोरदर्शनम् ॥१६॥
verses.english: In the case of some, we see that without any exertion on their part, what is not desired is not brought about and what is desired, is done. This then must be the result of Nature.

verses.sanskrit: तामृचीकस्तदा दृष्ट्वा तस्या गर्भगतं द्विजम् । अब्रवीद्भृगुशार्दूलः स्वां भार्यां देवरूपिणीम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: Some extraordinary persons again are seen, for though possessed of superior intelligence they have to seek wealth from others that are vulgar in features and gifted with little intelligence.

verses.sanskrit: मात्राऽसिव्यंसिता भद्रे चरुव्यत्यासहेतुना । भविष्यति हि ते पुत्रः क्रूरकर्माऽत्यमर्षणः ॥१८॥
उत्पत्स्यति च ते भ्राता ब्रह्मभूतस्तपोरतः । विश्वं हि ब्रह्म सुमहच्चरौ तव समाहितम् ॥१९॥
verses.english: Indeed, when all qualities, good or bad, enter a person impelled by Nature, what is there for one to boast (of his superior possessions)?

verses.sanskrit: क्षत्रवीर्यं च सकलं तव मात्रे समर्पितम् । विपर्ययेण ते भद्रे नैतदेवं भविष्यति ॥२०॥
verses.english: All these come from Nature. This is my seitled belief. Even Liberation and knowledge of self, in my view, originate from the same Source.

verses.sanskrit: मातुस्ते ब्राह्मणो भूयात्तव च क्षत्रियः सुतः । सैवमुक्ता महाभागा भर्त्रा सत्यवती तदा ॥२१॥
verses.english: In this world all fruits, good or bad, that attach themselves to persons, are considered as the outcome of acts. I shall now describe fully the subject of acts. Hear me.

verses.sanskrit: पपात शिरसा तस्मै वेपन्ती चाब्रवीदिदम् । नार्होऽसि भगवन्नद्य वक्तुमेवंविधं वचः । ब्राह्मणापसदं पुत्रं प्राप्स्यसीति हि मां प्रभो ॥२२॥
verses.english: As a crow, while eating some food, announces the presences of that food by its repeated cawing, similarly all our acts only proclaim the indications of Nature.

verses.sanskrit: ऋचीक उवाच । नैष संकल्पितः कामो मया भद्रे तथा त्वयि । उग्रकर्मा समुत्पन्नश्चरुव्यत्यासहेतुना ॥२३॥
verses.english: He who is acquainted with only the metamorphoses of Nature but not with Nature which is supreme and exist by herself, feels stupefication on account of his ignorance. He, however, who understands the difference between Nature and her metamorphoses is never stupefied.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यवत्युवाच । इच्छन् लोकानपि मुने सृजेथाः किं पुनः सुतम् । शामात्मकमृजुं पुत्रं दातुमर्हसि मे प्रभो ॥२४॥
verses.english: All things originate from Nature. On account of one's certain conviction about it, he would never be affected by pride or arrogance.

verses.sanskrit: ऋचीक उवाच । नोक्तपूर्वानृतं भद्रे स्वैरेष्वपि कदाचन । किमुताग्निं समाधाय मन्त्रवच्चरुसाधने ॥२५॥
verses.english: When I know the origin of all the ordinances of mortality and when I ain acquainted with the instability of all objects, I can not, O Shakra, indulge in grief. All this is endued with an end.

verses.sanskrit: दृष्टमेतत्पुरा भद्रे ज्ञातं च तपसा मया । ब्रह्मभूतं हि सकलं पितुस्तव कुलं भवेत् ॥२६॥
verses.english: Without attachments, without pride, without desire and hope, freed from all fetters, and dissociated from everything, I am passing my time happily, seeing that appearance and disappearance of all created objects.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यवत्युवाच । काममेवं भवेत्पौत्रो ममेह तव च प्रभो । शमात्मकमहं पुत्रं लभेयं जपतां वर ॥२७॥
verses.english: For one who is wise, who is self-controlled, who is contented, who is without desire and hope, and who sees all things with the light of self-knowledge, on trouble or anxiety exists, O Shakra.

verses.sanskrit: ऋचीक उवाच । पुत्रे नास्ति विशेषो मे पौत्रे च वरवर्णिनि । यथा त्वयोक्तं वचनं तथा भद्रे भविष्यति ॥२८॥
verses.english: I have no liking or aversion for either Nature or her changes. I do not see any one now who is my enemy nor any one who is mine own.

verses.sanskrit: वासुदेव उवाच । ततः सत्यवती पुत्रं जनयामास भार्गवम् । तपस्यभिरतं शान्तं जमदग्निं यतव्रतम् ॥२९॥
verses.english: I do not, O Shakra, at any time seek either heaven, or this world, or the nether regions. It is not the fact that there is no happiness in understanding the Soul. But the Soul, being dissociated from everything, cannot enjoy happiness. Hence I desire nothing.

verses.sanskrit: विश्वामित्रं च दायादं गाधिः कुशिकनन्दनः । यः प्राप ब्रह्मसमितं विश्वैर्ब्रह्मगुणैर्युतम् ॥३०॥
verses.english: Shakra said Tell me the means, O Prahlada, by which this kind of wisdom may be acquired and by which this kind of tranquillity may be made one's own. I pray you.'

verses.sanskrit: ऋचीको जनयामास जमदग्निं तपोनिधिम् । सोऽपि पुत्रं ह्यजनयज्जमदग्निः सुदारुणम् ॥३१॥
verses.english: Prahlada said 'By simplicity, by carefulness, by purifying the soul, by controlling the passions, and by waiting upon elders, O Shakra, a person acquires liberation.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वविद्यान्तगं श्रेष्ठं धनुर्वेदस्य पारगम् । रामं क्षत्रियहन्तारं प्रदीप्तमिव पावकम् ॥३२॥
verses.english: Know this, however, that one gains wisdom from Nature, and that the acquisition of tranquillity also is owing to the same cause. Indeed, everything else that you see is due to Nature.

verses.sanskrit: तोषयित्वा महादेवं पर्वते गन्धमादने । अस्त्राणि वरयामास परशुं चातितेजसम् ॥३३॥
verses.english: Thus addressed by the king of the Daityas, Shakra became filled with wonder and lauded those words, O king, with a cheerful heart.

verses.sanskrit: स तेनाकुण्ठधारेण ज्वलितानलवर्चसा । कुठारेणाप्रमेयेण लोकेष्वप्रतिमोऽभवत् ॥३४॥
verses.english: The king of the three worlds then, having adored the lord of the Daityas, took his leave and proceeded to his own quarter.'

verses.sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु कृतवीर्यात्मजो बली । अर्जुनो नाम तेजस्वी क्षत्रियो हैहयाधिपः ॥३५॥
verses.english: Meanwhile the powerful son of Kritavirya, the king of the Haihayas, endued with great power, highly pious, and possessed of a on thousand arms through the favour of the great Rishi) Dattatreya, having conquered in battle, by the strength of his own arms, the entire Earth with her mountains and seven islands, became a very powerful sovereign and (at iast) gave away the Earth to the Brahmanas in a house-sacrifice.

verses.sanskrit: दत्तात्रेयप्रसादेन राजा बाहुसहस्रवान् । चक्रवर्ती महातेजा विप्राणामाश्वमेधिके ॥३६॥
ददौ स पृथिवीं सर्वां सप्तद्वीपां सपर्वताम् । स्वबाह्वस्त्रबलेनाजौ जित्वा परमधर्मवित् ॥३७॥
तृषितेन च कौन्तेय भिक्षितश्चित्रभानुना । सहस्रबाहुर्विक्रान्तः प्रादाद्भिक्षामथाग्नये ॥३८॥
verses.english: Once begged by the thirsty god of fire, O son of Kunti, the thousand-armed king of great prowess gave alms to that deity.

verses.sanskrit: ग्रामान्पुराणि राष्ट्राणि घोषांश्चैव तु वीर्यवान् । जज्वाल तस्य बाणाग्राच्चित्रभानुर्दिधक्षया ॥३९॥
verses.english: Originating from the point of his arrow, the highly powerful god of fire, desirous of consuming (what was offered) burnt villages and towns and kingdoms and hamlets of cowherds.

verses.sanskrit: स तस्य पुरुषेन्द्रस्य प्रभावेण महौजसः । ददाह कार्तवीर्यस्य शैलानथ वनस्पतीन् ॥४०॥
verses.english: Through the prowess of that foremost of inen, viz., the powerful Kartavirya, the god of fire consumed mountains and great forests.

verses.sanskrit: स शून्यमाश्रमं रम्यमापवस्य महात्मनः । ददाह पवनेनेद्धश्चित्रभानुः सहैहयः ॥४१॥
verses.english: Helped by the king of the Haihayas the god of fire, increased more by the wind, consumed the uninhabited but the charming hermitage of the high-souled Apava.

verses.sanskrit: आपवस्तु ततो रोषाच्छशापार्जुनमच्युत । दग्धे श्रमे महाबाहो कार्तवीर्येण वीर्यवान् ॥४२॥
verses.english: O mighty-armed king, seeing his hermitage consumed by the powerful Kshatriya, the highly energetic Apava cursed that monarch in anger, saying,-Since, O Arjuna, without reserving these my woods, you have burnt them, therefore, Rama (of Bhrigu's race), will cut your thousand arins.

verses.sanskrit: त्वया न वर्जितं यस्मान्ममेदं हि महद्वनम् । दग्धं तस्माद्रणे रामो बाहूंस्ते च्छेत्स्यतेऽर्जुन ॥४३॥
अर्जुनस्तु महातेजा बली नित्यं शमात्मकः । ब्रह्मण्यश्च शरण्यश्च दाता शूरश्च भारत ॥४४॥
verses.english: The powerful Arjuna, however, of great prowess, always devoted to peace, ever obedient to Brahmanas and ready to protect all classes, and charitable brave, O Bharata, did not think of that curse imprecated on him by that great Rishi. His powerful sons, always proud and cruel, on account of that curse, became the indirect cause of his death. The princes, O foremost of Bharata's race, caught and brought away the calf of Jamadagani's Homa COW, against the knowledge of Kartavirya the king of the Haihayas. For this reason a dispute took place between the great Jamadagni and the Haihayas.

verses.sanskrit: नाचिन्तयत्तदा शापं तेन दत्तं महात्मना । तस्य पुत्रास्तु बलिनः शापेनासन्पितुर्वधे ॥४५॥
निमित्तादवलिप्ता वै नृशंसाश्चैव सर्वदा । जमदग्निधेन्वास्ते वत्समानिन्युर्भरतर्षभ ॥४६॥
अज्ञातं कार्तवीर्येण हैहेयेन्द्रेण धीमता । तन्निमित्तमभूद्युद्धं जामदग्नेर्महात्मनः ॥४७॥
ततोऽर्जुनस्य बाहूंस्तांश्छित्त्वा रामो रुषान्वितः । तं भ्रमन्तं ततो वत्सं जामदग्न्यः स्वमाश्रमम् ॥४८॥
verses.english: The powerful Rama, the son of Jamadagni, filled with anger cut off the arms of Arjuna and brought back, O king, his father's calf which was grazing within the inner appointment of the king's mansion.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यानयत राजेन्द्र तेषामन्तःपुरात्प्रभुः । अर्जुनस्य सुतास्ते तु सम्भूयाबुद्धयस्तदा ॥४९॥
गत्वाऽऽश्रममसम्बुद्धा जमदग्नेर्महात्मनः । अपातयन्त भल्लाग्रैः शिरः कायान्नराधिप ॥५०॥
verses.english: Then the foolish sons of Arjuna, going in a body to the hermitage of the great Jamadagni, cut with their lances, O king, the head of that Rishi from off his trunk while the celebrated Rama had gone out for fetching sacred fuel and grass.

verses.sanskrit: समित्कुशार्थं रामस्य निर्यातस्य यशस्विनः । ततः पितृवधामर्षाद्रामः परममन्युमान् ॥५१॥
निःक्षत्रियां प्रतिश्रुत्य महीं शस्त्रमगृह्वत । ततः स भृगुशार्दूलः कार्तवीर्यस्य वीर्यवान् ॥५२॥
verses.english: Worked up with anger at the death of his father and filled with vengeance, Rama vowed to rid the Earth of Kshatriyas and took up arms.

verses.sanskrit: विक्रम्य निजघानाशु पुत्रान्पौत्रांश्च सर्वशः । स हैहयसहस्राणि हत्वा परममन्युमान् ॥५३॥
verses.english: Then that foremost of the Bhrigus, endued with great energy, displaying his prowess, quickly killed all the sons and grandsons of Kartavirya.

verses.sanskrit: चकार भार्गवो राजन् महीं शोणितकर्दमाम् । स तथाऽऽशु महातेजाः कृत्वा निःक्षत्रियां महीम् ॥५४॥
verses.english: Killing thousand of Haihayas in anger, the descendant of Bhrigu, o king, covered the Earth with blood.

verses.sanskrit: कृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो वनमेव जगाम ह । ततो वर्षसहस्रेषु समतीतेषु केषुचित् ॥५५॥
verses.english: Highly energetic, he speedily freed the Earth of all Kshatriyas. Filled then with pity, he retired into the woods.

verses.sanskrit: क्षेपं सम्प्राप्तवांस्तत्र प्रकृत्या कोपन: प्रभुः । विश्वामित्रस्य पौत्रस्तु रैभ्यपुत्रो महातपाः ॥५६॥
verses.english: Afterwards, after the expiry of some thousands of years, the powerful Rama, who was angry by nature, was accused of cowardice.

verses.sanskrit: परावसुर्महाराज क्षिप्त्वाऽऽह जनसंसदि । ये ते ययातिपतने यज्ञे सन्तः समागताः ॥५७॥
verses.english: The grandson of Vishvamitra and son of Raivya, possessed of great ascetic merit, named Paravasu, O king, began to accuse Rama publicly, saying,-O Rama, were not those pious men, viz., Pratardana and others, who were assembled at a sacrifice at the time of Yayati's death, Kshatriyas by birth?

verses.sanskrit: प्रतर्दनप्रभृतयो राम किं क्षत्रिया न ते ॥५८॥
मिथ्याप्रतिज्ञो राम त्वं कत्थसे जनसंसदि । भयात्क्षत्रियवीराणां पर्वतं समुपाश्रितः ॥५९॥
verses.english: You are not truthful, O Rama! You simply brag before people. For fear of Kshatriya heroes you have betaken yourself to the mountains.

verses.sanskrit: सा पुनः क्षत्रियशतैः पृथिवी सर्वतः स्तृता । परावसोर्वचः श्रुत्वा शस्त्रं जग्राह भार्गवः ॥६०॥
verses.english: Hearing these words of Paravashu, the descendant of Bhrigu, once more took up arms and once more covered the Earth with hundreds of Kshatriya bodies.

verses.sanskrit: ततो ये क्षत्रिया राजन् शतशस्तेन वर्जिताः । ते विवृद्धा महावीर्याः पृथिवीपतयोऽभवन् ॥६१॥
verses.english: Those Kshatriyas, however, king counting by hundreds, that were not killed by Rama, multiplied (in time) and became powerful monarchs on Earth.
verses.bhavadeepa: स्तृता व्याप्ता शस्त्रं जग्राह तत्कार्यं क्षत्रियाणामन्तं कृतवान् ॥६०॥

verses.sanskrit: स पुनस्ताञ्जघानाशु बालानपि नराधिप । गर्भस्थैस्तु मही व्याप्ता पुनरेवाभवत्तदा ॥६२॥
verses.english: Rama once more killed them quickly, not sparing even the very children, O king. The Earth again was covered with the bodies of Kshatriya children of premature birth.

verses.sanskrit: जातं जातं स गर्भं तु पुनरेव जघान ह । अरक्षंश्च सुतान् कांश्चित्तदा क्षत्रिययोषितः ॥६३॥
verses.english: As soon as Kshatriya children were born, Rama killed them. Some Kshatriya ladies, however, succeeded in hiding their children from Rama.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिःसप्तकृत्वः पृथिवीं कृत्वा निःक्षत्रियां प्रभुः । दक्षिणामश्वमेधान्ते कश्यपायाददत्ततः ॥६४॥
verses.english: Having made the Earth shorn of Kshatriyas for twenty-one times, the powerful Bhargava, at the completion of a horse-sacrifice, gave away the Earth the Earth as sacrificial present to Kashyapa.

verses.sanskrit: स क्षत्रियाणां शेषार्थं करेणोद्दिश्य कश्यपः । स्रुक्प्रग्रहवता राजंस्ततो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ॥६५॥
verses.english: For preserving the residence of the Kshatriyas, Kashyapa, O king, pointing with his hand that still held the sacrificial ladle, said these words,-Ogreat sage, go to the shores of the southern ocean. You should not, O Rama, live within my kingdom.

verses.sanskrit: गच्छ तीरं समुद्रस्य दक्षिणस्य महामुने । न ते मद्विषये राम वस्तव्यमिह कर्हिचित् ॥६६॥
verses.bhavadeepa: स्रुक्प्रग्रहवता करेणेति कश्यपोऽध्वर्युः सन् कर्मान्तर एव माध्यन्दिनसवने दक्षिणाकाले इदं अब्रवीदिति सूच्यते ॥६५॥

verses.sanskrit: ततः शूर्पारकं देशं सागरस्तस्य निर्ममे । सहसा जामदग्न्यस्य सोऽपरान्तमहीतलम् ॥६७॥
verses.english: At these words, Ocean all on a sudden made for Jamadagni's son, on his other shore, a region called Surparaka.

verses.sanskrit: कश्यपस्तां महाराज प्रतिगृह्य वसुन्धराम् । कृत्वा ब्राह्मणसंस्थां वै प्रविष्टः सुमहद्वनम् ॥६८॥
verses.english: Kashyapa also, O king, having accepted the Earth in gift, and made a present of it to the Brahmanas, entered into woods.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शूद्राश्च वैश्याश्च यथा स्वैरप्रचारिणः । अवर्तन्त द्विजाग्र्याणां दारेषु भरतर्षभ ॥६९॥
अराजके जीवलोके दुर्बला बलवत्तरैः । पीड्यन्ते न हि विप्रेषु प्रभुत्वं कस्यचित्तदा ॥७०॥
verses.english: When anarchy begins on Earth, the weak are oppressed by the strong, and no man is master of his own possessions.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कालेन पृथिवी पीड्यमाना दुरात्मभिः । विपर्ययेण तेनाशु प्रविवेश रसातलम् ॥७१॥
verses.english: By the course of Time, the earth was assailed by wicked men. Unprotected duly by the virtuous Kshatriyas, and oppressed by the wicked for that disorder, the Earth quickly sank to the lowest depths.

verses.sanskrit: अरक्ष्यमाणा विधिवत्क्षत्रियैर्धर्मरक्षिभिः । तां दृष्ट्वा द्रवतीं तत्र संत्रासात्स महामनाः ॥७२॥
ऊरुणा धारयामास कश्यपः पृथिवीं ततः । धृता तेनोरुणा येन तेनोर्वीति मही स्मृता ॥७३॥
verses.english: Seeing the Earth sinking from fear, the great Kashyapa held her on his lap; and because the great Rishi held her on his lap (uru) therefore is the Earth known by the name of Urvi.

verses.sanskrit: रक्षणार्थं समुद्दिश्य ययाचे पृथिवी तदा । प्रसाद्य कश्यपं देवी वरयामास भूमिपम् ॥७४॥
verses.english: The goddess Earth for securing protection, pleased Kashyapa and begged of him a king.

verses.sanskrit: पृथिव्युवाच । सन्ति ब्रह्मन्मया गुप्ताः स्त्रीषु क्षत्रियपुङ्गवाः । हैहयानां कुले जातास्ते संरक्षन्तु मां मुने ॥७५॥
verses.english: The Earth said-There are, O Rishi, some leading Kshatriyas concealed by me among women. They were born in the family of the Haihayas. Let them, O sage, protect me.

verses.sanskrit: अस्ति पौरवदायादो विदूरथसुतः प्रभो । ऋक्षैः संवर्धितो विप्र ऋक्षवत्यथ पर्वते ॥७६॥
verses.english: There is another person of Puru's family, viz., Viduratha's son, O powerful one, who has been brought up among bears in the Rikshavat mountains.

verses.sanskrit: तथाऽनुकम्पमानेन यज्वनाऽथामितौजसा । पराशरेण दायादः सौदासस्याभिरक्षितः ॥७७॥
verses.english: Another, viz., the son of Saudasa, has been protected, through pity, by the highly energetic Parashara ever engaged in sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वकर्माणि कुरुते शूद्रवत्तस्य स द्विजः । सर्वकर्मेत्यभिख्यातः स मां रक्षतु पार्थिवः ॥७८॥
verses.english: Though born in the family of a twice-born one, yet like a Shudra he does everything for that Rishi and has, therefore been named servant of all work.

verses.sanskrit: शिबिपुत्रो महातेजा गोपतिर्नाम नामतः । वने संवर्धितो गोभिः सोऽभिरक्षतु मां मुने ॥७९॥
verses.english: Shivi's energetic son Gopati, has, been brought up in the forest among kine. Let him, O sage, protect me.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतर्दनस्य पुत्रस्तु वत्सो नाम महाबलः । वत्सैः संवर्धितो गोष्ठे स मां रक्षतु पार्थिवः ॥८०॥
verses.english: Pratradana's highly powerful son named Vatsa has been brought up among calves in a cowpen. Let that Kshatriya protect me.

verses.sanskrit: दधिवाहनपौत्रस्तु पुत्रो दिविरथस्य च । गुप्तः स गौतमेनासीद्गङ्गाकूलेऽभिरक्षितः ॥८१॥
verses.english: Dadhivahana's grandson and Diviratha's son was kept hidden on the banks of Ganga by the sage Gautama.

verses.sanskrit: बृहद्रथो महातेजा भूरिभूतिपरिष्कृतः । गोलाङ्गूलैर्महाभागो गृध्रकूटेऽभिरक्षितः ॥८२॥
verses.english: His name is Brihadratha. Possessed of great energy and endued with numerous accomplishments, that blessed princes has been protected by wolves and the mountains of Griddhrakuta.

verses.sanskrit: मरुत्तस्यान्ववाये च रक्षिता: क्षत्रियात्मजाः । मरुत्पतिसमा वीर्ये समुद्रेणाभिरक्षिताः ॥८३॥
verses.english: Many Kshatriyas of the race of Marutta have been protected. Equally energetic like the lord of Maruts, they have been brought up by Ocean.

verses.sanskrit: एते क्षत्रियदायादास्तत्र तत्र परिश्रुताः । द्योकारहेमकारादिजातिं नित्यं समाश्रिताः ॥८४॥
verses.english: These children of the Kshatriyas have been heard of as housing in different places. They are residing with artisans and goldsmiths. If they protect me I shall then remain unmoved.

verses.sanskrit: यदि मामभिरक्षन्ति ततः स्थास्यामि निश्चला । एतेषां पितरश्चैव तथैव च पितामहाः ॥८५॥
verses.bhavadeepa: द्योतुल्यान्विचित्रप्रासादादीन्कुर्वन्ति ते द्योकाराः शिल्पिनः ज्याकारेति पाठान्तरे स्पष्टोऽर्थः ॥८४॥

verses.sanskrit: मदर्थं निहता युद्धे रामेणाक्लिष्टर्मणा । तेषामपचितिश्चैव मया कार्या महामुने ॥८६॥
verses.english: Their fathers and grandfathers have been killed for my sake by the highly powerful Rama. It is my duty, O great sage, to see that their funeral rites are properly performed.

verses.sanskrit: न ह्यहं कामये नित्यमतिक्रान्तेन रक्षणम् । वर्तमानेन वर्तेयं तत्क्षिप्रं संविधीयताम् ॥८७॥
वासुदेव उवाच । ततः पृथिव्या निर्दिष्टांस्तान्समानीय कश्यपः । अभ्यषिञ्चन्महीपालान्क्षत्रियान्वीर्यसम्मतान् ॥८८॥
verses.english: Vasudeva said are Then finding out those energetic Kshatriyas whom the goddess had named, the sage Kashyapa installed them duly as kings.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च येषां वंशाः प्रतिष्ठिताः । एवमेतत्पुरावृत्तं यन्मां पृच्छसि पाण्डव ॥८९॥
verses.english: Those Kshatriya races that are now in existence the offsprings of those princes.-What you have questioned me son of Pandu, thus took place in days of yore.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवं ब्रुवंस्तं च यदुप्रवीरो युधिष्ठिरं धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठम् । रथेन तेनाशु ययौ महात्मा दिशः प्रकाशन्भगवानिवार्कः ॥९०॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said, Conversing thus with Yudhishthira, that foremost of pious men, the great Yadava hero proceeded quickly on thai car lighting up all the quarters like the divine Sun himself.
